messages.text:
Make two CI changes in Bifrost, in one PR with two commits. Read
.github/workflows/AGENTS.md and .agents/docs/scheduled-only-tests.md first.

## Commit 1: Move seven scheduled-only tests to the per-push suite

Remove the `#[cfg_attr(not(scheduled_tests), ignore = "scheduled-only")]`
line from these tests. Each one caused a long red stretch in hourly or
nightly CI between Sep 2 and Oct 8. Per-push CI passed on the same commits
only because it skipped the test.

| Test (nextest binary :: name) | Hourly failed runs / incidents |
|---|---|
| brokk-bifrost::suite_bench_policy bifrost_policy_cli::policy_suppressions_are_deterministic_auditable_and_threshold_aware_across_formats | 58 / 5 |
| brokk-bifrost::suite_bench_policy bifrost_policy_cli::thresholds_cover_clean_rated_and_unrated_findings | 58 / 5 |
| brokk-bifrost::suite_bench_policy bifrost_policy_cli::diff_base_narrows_the_gate_to_new_findings_across_formats | nightly 3 / 1 |
| brokk-bifrost-runtime::extension node_identity::byte_identical_siblings_get_distinct_stable_ids | 46 / 2 |
| brokk-bifrost-runtime::extension completion_states::a_frontier_under_generous_budgets_is_not_budget_truncation | 37 / 1 |
| brokk-bifrost-runtime::extension completion_states::an_exhausted_budget_names_the_dimension_it_exhausted | 37 / 1 |
| brokk-bifrost::suite_usages usage_graph_cpp_test::out_of_line_member_definition_qualifiers_edge_to_class | 41 / 1 |

Before you edit, check that per-push ci.yml actually runs each of these test
binaries on Linux x86. Look at the lane selection and impact
classification. If a binary is not selected on push, removing the attribute
does nothing for that test. In that case, stop and report it for that test
instead of changing ci.yml.

Then run each test without the cfg flag, using the normal target directory
and no RUSTFLAGS. Confirm that it runs rather than being skipped, that it
passes, and how long it takes. Report the passing time of each test. The
failing runs took between 0.1 and 7 seconds. If any test takes more than
about 10 seconds when it passes, keep it scheduled-only and tell me.

## Commit 2: Reduce the hourly matrix

Keep the hourly cron as it is.

1. In hourly.yml, remove the aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu entry from the
   `rust_matrix` of the os-matrix job. Add the same leg to the nightly.yml
   `rust_matrix`. Use the same RunsOn spec and `--cfg scheduled_tests`, but
   rename the runner label from `hourly-rust-arm64` to `nightly-rust-arm64`.
2. In hourly.yml, remove the aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu entry from
   `python_matrix`. Nightly already runs Python on Linux ARM64.
3. Do not touch the `arm-link-diagnostic` job. It is a manual, pinned-SHA
   diagnostic.
4. Keep the Windows x64 Rust leg and all other hourly legs.

Before you remove anything, search for consumers of the hourly job names or
the ARM legs. Check release-readiness, release-context, release.yml, the
nightly incident job, and the scripts under scripts/. RC qualification uses
hourly runs, so a check may expect an ARM64 hourly job to exist. If one
does, tell me what depends on it and propose a fix. Do not quietly drop a
release gate.

Update every description of the schedule to match the new setup. That
includes the header comments in hourly.yml and nightly.yml, the "schedule"
list in scheduled-only-tests.md, and any other place your search finds.
Validate the workflow YAML with actionlint if it is available.

## Handback

Report:
- the per-push lane that runs each promoted test, with its passing time
- any test you left scheduled-only, and why
- every consumer of the hourly ARM jobs you found, and what you did about it
- the validation you ran

The monitor expiring needs no action. I did find a mistake of my own, though. My summary and the pull request table say every time was measured with the test running alone, but I only did that for the three policy tests. The runtime and C++ times come from the first runs, where the three runtime tests ran together. I'll correct the pull request description.

I made a mistake in my summary and in the description of draft pull request #4742, and I have now fixed the description. Both said every passing time came from running the test alone. Only the policy tests were timed that way.

- **Three policy tests.** Each was timed alone, twice. The promoted policy test took 7 to 8 seconds. The two slow tests are the ones I kept scheduled-only.
- **Three runtime tests.** These ran together in one nextest run. Each took under a second.
- **C++ usage test.** This ran in its own run and took under a second. It was timed once, not twice.

None of these times is close to the 10-second limit, so all five promotions stand. The table in the pull request no longer says "alone". A note under the table now explains how each time was measured.

Nothing else has changed. The pull request is still a draft and still waits on your decision about the release-qualification gate. Merging it as is would make every release-candidate check fail on the missing hourly ARM64 jobs.
sorry, what's the decision?

The decision is how release qualification should check Linux ARM64 once those tests run only in nightly.

Today the release check requires a green hourly run with the Linux ARM64 Rust and Python jobs at the candidate's exact commit. After my change, hourly no longer has those jobs, so every release-candidate check would fail. The check needs a new source for that evidence, and there are three choices.

1. **Require only the Linux ARM64 jobs from nightly.** This is my recommendation. A candidate would need a nightly run at its exact commit with both Linux ARM64 jobs green, and the rest of nightly stays optional as it is today. This keeps the gate as strong as it is now. The cost is that a candidate must also get a nightly run, which you can start by hand the same way you start hourly for an RC.
2. **Require all of nightly.** This is simpler but stricter. It also makes Windows ARM64 and macOS hard release gates. For v0.13, Windows ARM64 has an owner exception because it fails, so this choice would block on it in the general release route.
3. **Stop requiring Linux ARM64 for releases.** This is the smallest change, but it drops a release gate. You told me not to do that quietly, so I would only do it if you choose it.

If you pick an option, I'll add it as a third commit to pull request #4742. The commit would update the job lists in `scripts/release-qualification.mjs` and `scripts/verify-projection-qualification.mjs` and their test fixtures. Then I'll mark the pull request ready.
i think we want all of nightly

I'll make nightly a required workflow for release qualification, move the two Linux ARM64 job names from the hourly list to the nightly list, and update the tests and release guidance. First I'll read how the gate treats nightly in each route.
The v0.13 route already requires nightly, with an owner exception for Windows ARM64. The general route treats nightly as optional. Let me read the test fixture and the guidance text I need to change.
The fixture uses positional run IDs, so I'll append nightly as the fifth run to keep existing indexes valid. Let me check whether the public release script keeps its own required-workflow list.
Only the two scripts hold job lists. Making the edits now.
Both groups are the expected fixture gaps: qualification now returns five pieces of evidence instead of four, and the v0.13 nightly fixture lacks the new Linux ARM64 Rust job. Updating the fixtures.
Nightly runs on the RC branch should be accepted when dispatched by hand. I'll make the RC test move nightly onto the RC branch too, so it covers that path, then update the counts.
All pass. The missing-workflow test now also removes the nightly run and confirms qualification is refused. I'll run the other tests that call into the qualification scripts.
Everything passes. Committing, merging current master, and pushing.
Master has not moved. Pushing, updating the pull request description, and marking it ready.

Release qualification now requires a complete nightly run, and pull request #4742 is marked ready for the merge queue.

The pull request now has three commits instead of the two you asked for, because the release-gate fix needed its own commit:

1. **Five tests now run on every push.** Two slow policy tests stay scheduled-only, as described before.
2. **The Linux ARM64 legs move from hourly to nightly.** The rest of hourly is unchanged.
3. **Nightly is now a required workflow for release qualification.**

What the third commit changes:

- **General release route.** Nightly is no longer optional. The two Linux ARM64 jobs moved from the hourly job list to the nightly list. Every nightly job must be green, so Windows ARM64 and macOS are now release gates too.
- **v0.13 route.** This route already required nightly. Its owner exception still lets a release go ahead when Windows ARM64 is the only failing nightly job. I kept that exception because it is a separate, documented owner decision. Under the exception, the Linux ARM64 Rust job must now also be green. If you meant "all of nightly" to remove that exception for v0.13 too, tell me and I'll take it out.
- **Release candidates.** A candidate now needs a nightly run at its exact commit. Nightly can be started by hand on RC branches, the same way hourly is.
- **Guidance.** The release guidance in `.agents/docs/release-and-open-core.md` now says nightly is required.

**Validation.**
- I updated the release tests. They now confirm that a missing nightly run blocks qualification, and that a nightly run started by hand on an RC branch is accepted.
- The release-qualification, projection-qualification, release-candidate and workflow shape tests all pass, along with the other release-script tests.
- Master had not moved when I pushed.
Dave asked us to tackle #4741
I'll start by reading the issue.
Let me orient in parallel: claim the issue, read my notes on the #4437 work, and get a first look at the code and related issues.
While the children work, I'll read the selection and receipt code myself since the design depends on it.
I have the selection and receipt flow. Next I need the manifest structs, the rest of the pair preparation, inventory loading, and the engine profile. Those are independent reads.
I now have the full picture of the current implementation. Let me collect the children's reports before settling the design.
While both children work, I'll checkpoint the plan on the branch so the design is recorded, then wait for reports.
Both children are still working after an hour, which is expected for a 5,000-line module rewrite plus a first test link. I'll keep waiting.
The drift check named a file none of us touched. I'll check whether that complaint pre-exists on master (and whether it is fatal), and keep waiting for the library child.
The drift complaint is pre-existing on master (the check exits 1 there too, from `83c429509f`), so it is not ours. I'll note it in the PR and continue waiting for the library child.
Now I'll review the library's core: the request types and failure mapping, the request validation, the selector, and the outcome builder. These are independent reads.
The library compiles. Now I'll update the outcome schema and docs for `selection.selection_reason` and the prerelease range rule, and hand the test fixes back to the matrix child.
B's CLI work compiles and `suite_mcp_cli` is green; `suite_bench_policy` has 14 failures that I need to classify (environment, transient, or ours). I'll read B's failure list now.
While validation runs, I'll review the two consequential pieces I have not yet read: B's CLI implementation and the docs chapter the service will read.
Validation is still in the bin clippy build (the merge pulled upstream crate changes, so it is a larger rebuild). I'll draft the PR description now so it is ready when validation finishes.

Validation (bin clippy, crate suite, CLI suites, bin tests, fmt) is running in the background after the master merge; the PR body is drafted with a validation placeholder. Next steps once it finishes: a live smoke of the built binary against the real public and premium repositories (expected typed `no-compatible-release`/`incompatible-strict-selection` outcomes on today's engine), then push and open the PR.
Waiting on the bin check (background task `b532cb540`) before committing; nothing else is independent of it. I'll proceed when it reports.
Bin compiles. Now commit, push with an explicit refspec (the `push.default=upstream` gotcha from my notes), and open the PR as ready: the work is complete and validated.

Done. PR #4749 is open and ready (not draft, base `master`), queued for MergeMarshall; a progress comment is on #4741.

## What landed

`bifrost prepare-open-packs` now takes a request document and always writes a typed outcome:

- **Request (v1):** root `pack_id` + repository, optional inventory pin, `selection` of mode `strict` (version + manifest digest; never substitutes) or `preferred` (preferred version, SemVer range, stable/prerelease channel), optional dependency pins. `PACK_SOURCE` keeps its meaning by converting to a strict public request.
- **One selector** for every path: candidates are checked in a fixed order and every rejection is recorded with a reason and detail. Premium-shaped roots (plain tags, ZIP, zero dependencies) select through the same code; a private 404 is `access-denied`, never an empty registry or public fallback.
- **Receipt v3** with an embedded strict `replay` request; **outcome v1** with 13 failure classes, `retryable`, engine identity and executable digest, the run's inventory snapshot and rejections; exit 0/1/2. JSON schemas in `schemas/`, docs chapter, and the CI action/workflow consumers updated.

## Validation

Post-merge with `origin/master`: bin and crate clippy clean; 88 crate tests, 113 `suite_mcp_cli`, 3 new CLI tests, 24 bin tests; fmt clean. A 53-case fake-registry matrix with golden outcomes validated against the schemas found and pinned three real selector defects before any live run (prerelease range matching, replay after an inventory refresh, order-dependent index digest). Live smoke against GitHub matched the contract in all six cases (public/premium preferred, premium strict, premium without token, no network), with no token in any output.

Two caveats, both pre-existing on master: the pack-authoring drift check fails on an unchanged Node notice file, and nine policy goldens differ on this host because of an installed Java pack.

## Still open on #4741

Publishing the interface in a checksum-verifiable release and consumer-contract tests against that executable are release work with #4709 (v0.13.1). On today's engine profile nothing can select; every live case correctly ends in a typed incompatibility. I left the issue open and assigned.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The selection identity deliberately excludes constraints, reason, and the inventory snapshot: a strict *replay* of a preferred-mode selection must land on the same cache directory and reuse verified bytes. Warm reuse compares content identity only; the run's own snapshot lives in the outcome, the original's in the immutable receipt.
- `semver::VersionReq` follows Cargo's rule that prerelease versions only match a comparator that itself names a prerelease, so `"*"` silently excludes every `-rc`. Matching the range against the base version and letting the channel decide prerelease admission keeps the two concerns separate.
- The fake-registry matrix paid for itself before the live run: three of the four defects it found were in replay/reproducibility paths that a live smoke against a stable registry cannot exercise.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
